result:
PLAT-103 is live. `validateApp` now throws when `owner` is missing or empty. All three apps pass their owner and still start. PR #1 went through CI and merged to `main`, and CD succeeded. I didn't start any app myself.

- **Owners:** billing passes `payments`, reports passes `insights`, and core-shell passes `platform`, each taken from the app's `package.json` `team` field.
- **Reports app:** `apps/sub-route-reports` also calls `validateApp` but wasn't in the ticket, so I added a sub-task for it and fixed it in the same PR.
- **One PR instead of three:** `libs/shared-contracts` lives in the repo and is inlined into the apps at build time. There is no registry release or lockfile bump to adopt. I put all the changes in one PR because the new check would have broken any app that landed without its owner. I bumped the library's version to 2.0.0 to mark the breaking change, though nothing publishes it.
- **Stray sub-task:** I accidentally created a sub-task titled "--help" by running `st task add --help`. I marked it done, since I couldn't find a way to delete it.
- **Shell quoting:** my first `sed` commands failed on macOS quoting, so I switched to `perl`. That cost one retry.
